metadata.title: The Global Renewable Electricity Transition and Its Decoupling from CO2 Emissions: A Reproducible Cross-Country Analysis, 2000-2022
metadata.description: Empirical study of 163 countries (2000-2022, 3,749 country-year observations) on whether the renewable electricity transition is decoupling GDP from CO2 emissions, and whether renewables displace or merely add to fossil generation. Methods: beta/sigma convergence, Tapio decoupling index, two-way fixed-effects panel of CO2 per capita on renewable share (with lagged-renewable, first-difference, and country-clustered-robustness checks), a second outcome (CO2 intensity of electricity) that tests displacement directly, a country-level event study, and an absolute-generation displacement accounting decomposed by region. Headline results: +1 pp renewable share implies ~0.4% lower CO2/capita and ~2.2% lower grid carbon intensity, but the world added ~5,600 TWh renewables alongside ~7,900 TWh fossil generation, and only 31% of countries cut fossil output. Fully reproducible: src/analysis.py -> results.json -> report.html/dashboard.html.
references: Tapio, P. (2005). Towards a theory of decoupling. Transport Policy 12(2):137-151.
OECD (2002). Indicators to measure decoupling of environmental pressure from economic growth.
IPCC (2022). Climate Change 2022: Mitigation of Climate Change.
